topics.topic: Whether A01 repeat-success branches apply only after refusal and archive checks pass
questions: Must A01-3 apply only after the refusal guard of A01-2 is false, so that an equal-facts retry failing an earlier check cannot also be required to answer the record?
Are A01-3 and A01-4 conditional on A01-2 being false, or do their implications apply independently? The invariant must make the ordered or mutually exclusive branches explicit.
Must A01-3 apply only after every preliminary check and the archive check have passed, so that an equal-facts repeat cannot both be refused by A01-2 and answer the record under A01-3?

a check of stages (1) to (4) of A04 rule 6 fails, or m in {Room,
  ArtifactPointer} with its project archived => refused, store unchanged   -- A01-2
f = current_facts(r)  => answer r, store unchanged   -- A01-3
judgement.divergence: For an equal-facts retry of an existing pointer on an archived project, A01-2 requires refusal while A01-3 independently requires returning the pointer; Cabinet Kernel observes refusal versus a pointer answer.
judgement.why: The two unguarded implications apply to the same admissible equal-facts retry on an archived project and prescribe incompatible outcomes, despite the normative rules indicating that the refusal checks should take precedence.
options: Make A01-3 and A01-4 conditional on all A01-2 refusal conditions being false.
State explicitly that the displayed clauses are ordered cases with A01-2 taking precedence.
consequences: Without an explicit guard or ordering, an archived or unauthorized equal-facts retry is simultaneously required to be refused and answered.

events: The agent, through Cabinet Kernel, retries publishing the pointer on P with request id k and facts f.
outcomes: A01-2 refuses the retry and leaves the store unchanged because the project is archived.
A01-3 answers the existing pointer and leaves the store unchanged because the supplied facts equal its current facts.
witness.observer: Cabinet Kernel, and through it the agent, sees either a refusal or the pointer record.
basis:
An artifact pointer is such a link — "this project has this document
of that service" — so the agent publishes and withdraws pointers through
Kernel, on a project its session is granted (R0-46), and the owner does in the
owner interface.

Archiving a project freezes its
pointers: publishing and withdrawing on it are refused, reading stays open
(R0-03).

As a write of the agent,
a publish carries a request id (R0-36, R0-78): a retry that is still allowed —
the project still in the session's set and not archived — returns the pointer
it made, whatever its status now; a retry no longer allowed is refused as any
call (R0-46, R0-17); and a new publish with equal content is still a new
version (R0-17).

topics.topic: How the security review must address A09 rule 4's changed refusal and undo guarantee
questions: How must this review account describe and assess the shown replacement of A09's normative refusal rule, which changes both its scope and removes the explicit guarantee that a change is undone?
Must the review record acknowledge and assess the changed normative guarantee in A09 rule 4, or must A09 be restored to a wording whose guarantee is unchanged from the closed version?

quotes:

   `personal_data` (R0-26). An answer that would carry a class above the
   token's highest is refused whole; Registry never answers part of it.

5. An answer that would carry a class above the calling token's highest is
   refused whole: no field of it is disclosed (rule 4).
judgement.why: A09 rule 4 is verbatim unchanged between the closed and current texts; the reopening added an invariant identifier, a required test, and witness bindings, so there is no replaced refusal scope or removed undo guarantee for A21 to assess.
options: Keep the accurate statement that no normative rule changed.
Revise the review only if A09's normative wording is actually changed.
consequences: No State 2 text change is required for the alleged replacement because it did not occur.

topics.topic: Whether A21 prohibits opening any listener before all A17 startup steps succeed or only serving requests
questions: Does this mean no listener is ever opened before every start check has passed, or only that no listener serves requests before all checks pass? It must agree with A17 rule 2, which opens the owner listener before attempting the service API listener and closes it if the latter fails.
Does the guarantee cover only checks performed before listener opening, or must even a failure while opening the second listener occur without any listener having been opened?

quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37). The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start:

last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.

Each start check that fails — a configuration item, a backup location that
    cannot be written, an existing store failing its integrity check or of
    another version, a new store that cannot be made — stops the start with no
    listener opened and no request served.
judgement.why: P1 already judged the same question on unchanged passages: the no-listener-opened guarantee covers the enumerated pre-listener failures, while a listener-opening failure may transiently open an earlier listener that is then closed without serving.

precedent.topic: Meaning and coverage of the no-listener-opened guarantee after a failed start check
quotes:
Registry checks the configuration when it starts and serves nothing until
   every check passes; a failed check stops the start with a diagnostic that
   names the failed item and never its value (R0-37). The checks run in one
   order and the first that fails stops the start:

last, the
   listener of each surface opened at its configured address (rule 1) — the
   owner interface's first, then the
   service API's unless the start is owner-only, one that cannot be opened
   failing the start and closing the one already opened.

Each start check that fails — a configuration item, a backup location that
    cannot be written, an existing store failing its integrity check or of
    another version, a new store that cannot be made — stops the start with no
    listener opened and no request served.
precedent.why: Required test 10 expressly enumerates only the four pre-listener failure classes, and rule 2 places all listener opening after those checks, so none has ever opened in the histories that item covers; listener-opening failure separately requires closing any listener already opened.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
State 2: decide required results and constraints, including necessary refusal precedence; carry test mechanisms, exact contracts and deployment procedures to their owners.
